verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. The Lean active set is the paper's A_ℓ with the clause 0 < q < q_big removed. activeReference (PrimaryRepresentatives.lean:412) is written directly in the slow coordinates (R,Z,T) and names the ratio q/Q as its bound variable: `∃ q ∈ Icc (1/2) 2` is 1/2 ≤ q/Q ≤ 2, `0 ≤ p.2.2` is τ ≥ 0, `forwardScalar (2h) Z q̂ = T` is the paper's q − z²q^{2h} = τ (p. 7, after (3.2)) divided by Q using 2D + 2h = 1, and `p.1^2/(2*q) ∈ Icc a b` is X_a ≤ r²/(2q) ≤ X_b; referenceCompact (:420) is its closure. physicalMask_normalized_mem (:502) proves that a physical point satisfying these clauses and lying in band L maps under the chart (normalizedSlow_coordinates, :495) into referenceCompact, so every point of the paper's A_ℓ lies in the Lean set. The converse fails for the bands at the cut-off. No clause of activeReference or hypothesis of physicalMask_normalized_mem bounds q by q_big, and the clause is not scale-invariant, so the single band-independent Lean set cannot carry it. With Q_ℓ = 2^{-ℓ} (SlotColoring.dyadicQ) and q_big ≤ 2^{-ℓ_0}, the paper's A_{ℓ_0} keeps only q < q_big ≤ Q_{ℓ_0}, whereas the Lean set keeps the whole range q/Q ∈ [1/2,2]; the two agree only for bands with 2Q_ℓ < q_big, where the clause is vacuous by arithmetic. The Lean does have a q_big (ActualCandidateConstruction.qbig = Q(firstBand), :155) and the arithmetic fact that bands from firstBand+1 on with q/Q < 2 lie below it (nativeScale_lt_qbig, :180), and it restricts labels by a lower band index (BaseChartJets.CellIndex, :825), but none of these is a clause of the set used to select labels, so the Lean label family is a superset of the paper's near the lowest bands. I did not trace how the index threshold in PrimaryGeometryAssembly.Index relates to firstBand, nor that the a, b arguments (NominalConeAssembly.activeLeft/activeRight) equal the paper's X_a, X_b. Minor further differences: Lean adds 0 ≤ R, and the labels are actually selected against referenceCompact ∩ {T > 0} (PositiveRepresentatives.positivePart), which concerns (6.8) rather than this display.
